request.spec:
A steward can waive a claim's late charge (a button on an OPEN or PENDING claim; CLAIM_WAIVED
naming the claim; anyone else, any other status, or a claim already waived is refused with an error
on the claim). A waived claim bears no late charge from then on, whatever its overdue state; show
waived yes/no on the claim.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can waive a claim's late charge (a button on an OPEN or PENDING claim; CLAIM_WAIVED
naming the claim; anyone else, any other status, or a claim already waived is refused with an error
on the claim). A waived claim bears no late charge from then on, whatever its overdue state; show
waived yes/no on the claim.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Stewards can now waive a claim's late charge. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What I changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V82__claim_waived.sql` adds a `waived` column to claims (default false). The `Claim` entity carries the flag and copies it when a claim is copied.
- **Server:**
  - A new endpoint, `POST /claims/{id}/waive`, which `ClaimService.waive` handles. It refuses anyone who isn't a steward, any claim that isn't OPEN or PENDING, and a claim that's already waived. A refused waive writes nothing.
  - A successful waive writes `CLAIM_WAIVED sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=… number=…`, plus the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines if any totals changed.
  - `LateCharge` now gives a waived claim no late charge, whatever its overdue state. The floor still applies.
- **Front end:** each claim shows a "Waived" yes/no value and a "Waive late charge" button, and a refusal shows on that claim's error element. The front end also works out the late charge itself, so I changed that calculation to skip waived claims too.

**One fix outside the request:** the last test kept failing because of an existing bug in the claim editor. When a user's attempt to edit a claim was refused because someone else held it, their claim form stayed attached to that claim. After the claim was opened and settled, adding a claim from that form was sent as an edit of the settled claim. The refusal then showed on the claim row instead of on the form, so the test timed out. I changed `editingId` in `person-claims.ts` so the editor closes once its claim is no longer a draft, unless the claim is due inside a closed period, where the existing read-only editor still opens. That follows the existing rule that closes the editor when its claim moves to another person.

I didn't make waiving refuse claims inside a closed period, because the request doesn't mention it. Re-dating a claim does refuse there, so add the same check to waiving if you want them to match.
